$comment: The one place the product's identity lives. Every other file reads these values (Node side: shared/config.mjs; extension side: the generated extension/lib/config.js). Change a value here, then run `npm run sync-config` so the extension copy and the manifest follow. `npm run rename -- <slug> "<Display Name>"` sets all of them at once.
tagline: Drive your real, logged-in browsers from any AI agent
$comment.nativeHostId: The Chromium native messaging host name. Lowercase letters, digits, dots and underscores only. It is written into the host manifest at install time and called by the extension's connectNative(); the two must match, which is why both read it from here.
$comment.socketName: The broker's local endpoint. On Windows this is the named pipe \\.\pipe\<socketName>; on macOS and Linux it is the file <stateDir>/<socketName>.sock. Never a TCP port: nothing in this system listens on the network.
$comment.stateDirName: Folder name for machine state (runtime token, route registry, audit log, screenshots, launcher). Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\<stateDirName>. macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/<stateDirName>. Linux: $XDG_STATE_HOME/<stateDirName> or ~/.local/state/<stateDirName>. Override the whole path with the BRIDGE_HOME environment variable.
$comment.serviceName: The always-on broker's supervisor entry: the Windows Task Scheduler task name, the launchd label suffix on macOS (<nativeHostId>.broker), and the systemd user unit name on Linux (<serviceName>-broker).
$comment.mcpServerName: The key written into your agent's MCP config (~/.claude.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codex/config.toml). Tool names are fixed (browser_*, bridge_*) and do not change with this.
